correctness.rationale: Exact columns give I-B*B=R-epsilon rr*, with R compact positive and r in ell2. The Birman-Schwinger sum is continuous strictly decreasing (infinite at zero, zero at infinity), so the sole negative eigenvalue is simple. A digamma sum and uniform asymptotics prove delta=exp(-1/epsilon-psi(2-epsilon))(1+o(1)). Riemann sums prove the complete rescaled mode law. Finite-dimensional congruence gives the exact first-negative compression and its sharp reciprocal relation to delta. B M=M* follows on a dense subset from the finite-support right inverse, giving exactly one negative eigenvalue in the compact self-commutator. The numerical checker supplements but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The primary full text proves the qualitative shift threshold and finite-rank defect but does not supply the unique negative spectral root, exponential prefactor, finite-section detection horizon or eigenvector mass limit. The closest general-order result treats the weighted relative self-commutator quotient, which is minus infinity at negative shift and cannot imply the finite auxiliary eigenvalue magnitude. The other close result concerns a different real-variable Cesaro perturbation. Broader rank-one binding principles remain a qualified priority risk.
residual_risks: General theorems for rank-one perturbations of compact harmonic diagonal operators may contain equivalent weak-coupling asymptotics under different language.

value.rationale: The established shift-hyponormality transition creates a natural exact spectral quantity: the negative eigenvalue of the bounded compact interrupter defect. The exponential e^{-1/epsilon} scale and its prefactor explain why every power-series perturbation and all initial coordinate tests below an exponentially large cutoff miss the instability. A sharp first-detection dimension and an explicit probability limit describe the hidden negative vector. These give a motivated complete boundary mechanism beyond correctness of a textbook rank-one test.
